papers.summary: Spectral weight decay applies a post-step nuclear-norm update. In LLaMA models, it lowers effective rank and improves SVD-LLM compression under matched validation-loss budgets.
papers.relevance: Directly addresses training for low-rank compressibility, spectral regularization, and label-noise generalization.

evidence.quote: Across 124 124 M to 500 500 M LLaMA models trained with Adam-family optimizers, the resulting low-effective-rank structure improves post-training compression under matched validation-loss budgets.

papers.title: Spectral Weight Decay: Inducing Low-Rank Structure in Neural Network Weights

papers.summary: Monarch–Muon combines structured weight factors with Muon. Its 6.89B systems benchmark reports lower peak memory and full-step time than dense Muon, while complete quality runs are at smaller scales.
papers.relevance: A concrete quality–memory–speed study of structured LLM pretraining.

evidence.quote: At 6.89B, Monarch–Muon reduces the full-step time by 45% and peak memory by 23% relative to dense Muon.
These benchmarks measure the cost of the training operations at larger widths, while the complete pretraining runs test learning quality.

papers.title: Monarch-Muon: Structure-Aware Muon for Fast and Memory-Efficient Pretraining

papers.summary: Ori tracks drifting gradient subspaces for low-rank LLM optimization. At rank 32 in a 1B LLaMA benchmark, its reported optimizer-step peak memory is 0.2487 GB versus GaLore's 0.3385 GB; that measure is not total training peak memory.
papers.relevance: Directly informs low-rank-gradient pretraining and the quality–memory–speed tradeoff.

evidence.quote: For instance, at rank 32, Ori requires only 0.2487 GB, which is 12.1% less than OSD (0.2832 GB) and 26.5% less than GaLore (0.3385 GB).
Our goal is to record the peak memory usage, incurred solely by the said optimizer’s update step.

papers.title: Ori: Drift-Aware Streaming $k$-PCA for Very Low-Rank LLM Training

papers.summary: Clean uses Nyström-sketched curvature preconditioning; Q-Clean compresses its states further. Matched 1.3B pretraining results report perplexity, optimizer memory, and peak memory against AdamW, SOAP, and Muon.
papers.relevance: Provides measured optimizer-state, total-memory, quality, and wall-clock tradeoffs for LLM pretraining.

evidence.quote: Clean reaches AdamW’s final performance in 64 hours instead of 81, while simultaneously reducing the optimizer memory footprint.

papers.title: Clean: Second-order LLM Training at Linear Memory Cost via Nystr{ö}m Sketching

papers.summary: A module-matched LoRA rank sweep under label noise finds a second descent, but tested post-peak ranks that still save parameters do not match dense fine-tuning risk.
papers.relevance: Directly tests rank-dependent memorization and generalization with an explicit dense baseline, including a 7B language model.

evidence.quote: Across four vision backbones and a 7 7 B language model, no measured post-peak rank that still saves parameters reaches dense, and the first equivalence result sits at four times dense’s projection weights under a single shared learning rate.

papers.title: LoRA's Second Descent Extends Beyond Parameter Parity

papers.summary: ORCA applies soft orthogonality regularization early in LLM training and then removes it. Reported validation-loss gains over Muon span LLaMA, Qwen3, and MoE settings.
papers.relevance: Tests how temporary spectral shaping affects optimization without permanently constraining the weight spectrum.

evidence.quote: In most experiments, the reduction is 0.02–0.04, comparable to or greater than Muon’s gain over Adam.
Due to computational budget constraints, we focus our comparison on Muon and ORCA.

papers.title: ORCA: The Annealed Spectral Conditioning Optimizer for Faster, Better LLM Training

papers.summary: BMuon changes Muon's update geometry to allocate a shared budget across MLP channels. In a 1B LLaMA-style experiment, it withstands heavy channel pruning, but has worse unpruned perplexity than Muon.
papers.relevance: Directly connects matrix-optimizer geometry to training-time structured compressibility, with a consequential quality tradeoff.

evidence.quote: On the unpruned models, Muon achieves lower perplexity ( 10.92 10.92 versus 12.84 12.84 for BMuon), but its performance degrades rapidly under pruning.
In contrast, BMuon preserves its unpruned performance up to 80 % 80\% pruning, reaching 12.86 12.86 with activation ranking and 12.85 12.85 with μ \mu ranking.

papers.title: BMuon: Budgeting Muon's Spectral Geometry for Structured Compressibility

papers.summary: A theoretical analysis relates frozen-feature bottleneck rank to low-rank minimizers under trace-norm regularization and examines factorized LoRA with weight decay. Its first-order rank-deficiency result does not rule out spurious local minima.
papers.relevance: Connects nuclear-norm regularization and low-rank LoRA geometry without NTK linearization.

evidence.quote: This is a first-order exclusion theorem, not a no-spurious-local-minima theorem; Proposition 4.9 gives an explicit limitation.
Trace-norm regularization then selects a low-rank representative among all matrices that induce the same observed output.

papers.title: How Finite-Rank Bottlenecks Shape the Low-Rank Adaptation Landscape

papers.summary: CORE is a training-free research-agent harness that retrieves passages but returns short, reranked snippets, with source expansion and deduplication. A controlled BrowseComp-Plus ablation reports 80.12% answer accuracy for full CORE versus 70.84% for search without context management.
papers.relevance: Offers a tested retrieval and context-management design for a handwritten digest harness.

evidence.quote: Coarse retrieval only 62.61 Coarse-to-fine search tool only 70.84 Full CORE 80.12
To ensure reproducibility, we restrict the study to closed search over fixed corpora.

papers.title: CORE: Coarse-to-Fine Search with Context Management for Deep Research

papers.summary: IDEA2PRIOR combines multi-source discovery, identity verification, facet-based assessment, citation expansion, and expert ranking to retrieve papers from informal research ideas.
papers.relevance: Directly matches the digest agent's auditable paper-retrieval and relevance-ranking goal.

evidence.quote: It combines multi-source discovery, identity verification, facet-based abstract assessment, semantic citation expansion, and joint Expert ranking.

papers.title: Idea2Prior: Auditable Paper Retrieval and Ranking from Research Ideas

limitations: IDEA2PRIOR's detailed evaluation controls were not inspected; inclusion rests on its described retrieval workflow rather than a verified performance advantage.
CORE was evaluated in closed search over fixed corpora, so transfer to this digest workflow is unverified.
BMuon's reported compression benefit is structured MLP-channel pruning, not low-rank SVD compression, and its unpruned language-model quality is worse than Muon's.
The larger-scale Monarch–Muon results are systems measurements, not complete pretraining quality runs.
Code availability, independent reproducibility, and X attention were not assessed.
